> **What this case shows** — spectrum and autocorrelation describe *when* a signal varies; the
> **amplitude distribution** describes *how its values are spread* — its **skewness** (asymmetry) and
> **kurtosis** (tailedness). These are the everyday tools for flagging EEG artifacts and checking the
> normality that downstream methods assume. This case adds them (**`signalMoments`**). On a real
> eyes-closed EEG channel it reproduces **`scipy.stats.skew` / `kurtosis`** (and numpy mean/std)
> **bit-for-bit** (max |diff| ~**4e-16**), and the verdict is: the amplitude distribution is
> **approximately Gaussian** (skewness −0.23, excess kurtosis +0.16).

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `signalMoments(x)` → mean, SD, skewness, excess kurtosis.
**Way of thinking** — the first two moments (mean, SD) set the scale; the next two set the *shape*.
Skewness ≈ 0 and excess kurtosis ≈ 0 means "Gaussian enough"; a large positive kurtosis is the
fingerprint of a spike or ocular artifact riding on the EEG.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioAnalysis::signalMoments()`.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed POz EEG, `signalMoments` reproduces `scipy.stats.skew` / `kurtosis` and numpy
mean/std bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~4e-16); the distribution is approximately Gaussian (skewness −0.23,
excess kurtosis +0.16).

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and a check: the ecosystem had spectral, autocorrelation and entropy views but
no amplitude-shape moments — can we author them, reproduce scipy.stats exactly, and characterize the
EEG's amplitude distribution?** The goal is to introduce `signalMoments`, certify it bit-for-bit, and
read the shape.

## Challenge & approach

The moments are mean, population SD (ddof = 0), skewness = E[(x−μ)³]/σ³, and excess kurtosis =
E[(x−μ)⁴]/σ⁴ − 3. We compute them and check against `scipy.stats.skew` (biased), `scipy.stats.kurtosis`
(Fisher/excess, biased) and numpy on the identical signal.

```
EEG POz (eegmmidb) → mean, sd(pop), skew = E[(x-mu)^3]/sd^3, exkurt = E[(x-mu)^4]/sd^4 - 3
                    vs scipy.stats.skew / kurtosis + numpy → bit-exact (~4e-16)
                    skew -0.23 (mild left tail), exkurt +0.16 (near-mesokurtic) -> approximately Gaussian
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **POz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked vector the EEG complexity and
time-series cases use. Details in [`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

Right: the four moments from PhysioAnalysis (red dots) and scipy.stats / numpy (green rings) — coincident at machine precision (max |diff| ~4e-16).](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the left panel is the shape (amplitude ≈ Gaussian); the right panel is the
certification (moments equal scipy.stats).

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **mean** | **0.24 µV** |
| **SD** (population) | **48.8 µV** |
| **skewness** | **−0.23** (mild left tail) |
| **excess kurtosis** | **+0.16** (near-mesokurtic) |
| op vs `scipy.stats` / numpy (max \|diff\|) | **4e-16** (bit-exact) |
| approximately Gaussian | **yes** |

The newly-authored op equals scipy.stats for all four moments, and the distribution is near-Gaussian.
Values trace to [`artifacts/moments_summary.csv`](artifacts/moments_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`signalMoments` adds the amplitude-shape view to the ecosystem's spectral, autocorrelation and entropy
descriptors, and it is exact: bit-for-bit against scipy.stats. The transferable takeaway: **check the
shape, not just the spectrum. Skewness and kurtosis near zero say the amplitudes are Gaussian enough for
the methods that assume it — and a kurtosis that suddenly spikes is your earliest, cheapest artifact
detector.**

## Open questions

- Kurtosis is a standard automatic EEG artifact detector (spiky/ocular artifacts drive it well above 0);
  running `signalMoments` per epoch and flagging high-kurtosis epochs would turn this descriptor into a
  quality-control layer, with a formal normality test (Shapiro-Wilk / Jarque-Bera) as the confirmatory
  companion. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Distribution moments (mean/SD/skew/kurtosis) | `signalMoments()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Autocorrelation / spectrum | `autocorrelation()`, `arSpectrum()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Choosing and reading the moments.**

- **skewness** — 0 is symmetric; negative = a longer left tail, positive = a longer right tail.
- **excess kurtosis** — 0 is Gaussian; positive = heavier tails / more peaked (leptokurtic; large values
  flag spiky artifacts), negative = lighter tails (platykurtic).
- **convention** — matches `scipy.stats.skew` (biased) and `scipy.stats.kurtosis` (Fisher / excess,
  biased) with the population SD (ddof = 0).

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

m <- signalMoments(x)
m$skewness; m$kurtosis                        # asymmetry and (excess) tailedness
abs(m$skewness) < 0.5 && abs(m$kurtosis) < 1  # approximately Gaussian?
# reproduces scipy.stats.skew / kurtosis (biased) and numpy mean / std bit-for-bit.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/moments_summary.csv`](artifacts/moments_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks
the skewness and kurtosis, the bit-exact scipy.stats / numpy match over all four moments, the
approximately-Gaussian verdict, the mean and SD, and the honestly-noted scope (newly-authored op;
machine-precision; biased/population conventions).
